# Session Recorder

> Session Recorder is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) Chrome extension for QA
> and product teams. Record a bug in the browser, annotate the exact element or
> area, and file a GitHub issue in one action with an AI-written summary and a
> link to a login-protected report.

Key facts: recording, annotation, local storage and ZIP export work without
any account, subscription or developer-operated server. Recordings are stored
in the browser (IndexedDB). Redaction of authorization headers, cookies,
token-like fields, sensitive URL parameters and password inputs is on by
default at capture time; it does not catch everything, so review evidence
before sharing. Optional integrations use the user's own credentials and send
data directly to those services: AI summaries and session names (OpenAI,
OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Anthropic, Google Gemini), voice transcription
(Deepgram, OpenAI, ElevenLabs; also used for spoken annotation comments,
with an optional page-vocabulary hint built by the configured model from
visible interface labels), report publishing (the user's Cloudflare
Pages project behind Cloudflare Access) and issue filing (GitHub). Those
providers' charges and limits apply. Exports are ZIP files containing
report.md, session.json, MANIFEST.md, transcript.json and assets (plus an
optional standalone report.html), at four detail levels (Full, Standard,
Compact, Minimal). Developed by Mohsen
Azimi.

## Product

- [Overview](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/): Free open-source Chrome extension for QA and product teams. Record a bug, annotate the exact element, and file a GitHub issue with an AI summary and a protected report link.
- [Chrome Web Store listing](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/session-recorder/dboiheheijgmfpfhbmjggiijpgondghh): install the extension.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/mohsen1/session-recorder-chrome-extension): source code, issues and README. AGPL-3.0.
- [Privacy Policy](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/privacy.html): Privacy policy for the Session Recorder Chrome extension. Recordings stay local by default. Optional transcription, AI summaries, and report publishing send data to services you configure.

## Features

- [All features](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/): Everything Session Recorder does: browser recording, live annotations, screenshots and video, voice notes, AI issue summaries, GitHub filing, protected publishing, redaction and exports.
- [Browser recording](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/browser-recording/): Record a bug reproduction in Chrome with interactions, console errors, network requests and responses, and tabs the app opens, all on one timeline. Free and open source.
- [Annotations](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/annotations/): Annotate the live page while recording: click an element or drag a freeform rectangle and type a comment. Numbered pins lead the report and the AI issue summary.
- [Screenshots and video](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/screenshots-video/): Session Recorder takes screenshots at every interaction, at key moments or on demand, skips near-duplicate frames, and can record the tab as video with audio.
- [Voice notes and transcription](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/voice-notes/): Narrate a bug while you record it. Audio stays local; add your own Deepgram, OpenAI or ElevenLabs key to get a timestamped transcript on the timeline.
- [AI issue summaries](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/ai-summaries/): Generate a GitHub issue title and summary from a recorded bug with your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or OpenAI-compatible model. Annotations lead; diagnostics support.
- [One-click GitHub issues](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/github-issues/): Choose File GitHub issue on a recorded bug: the extension summarizes it, publishes a protected report and creates the issue with a link. Multiple repositories, scoped tokens.
- [Protected report publishing](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/protected-publishing/): Share a recorded bug as a web report hosted in your own Cloudflare Pages project. Readers sign in through Cloudflare Access, and a Pages Function checks every request.
- [Local storage and redaction](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/privacy-redaction/): Session Recorder stores recordings in your browser and masks auth headers, cookies, token-like fields and password inputs as they are captured. What leaves, and when.
- [Exports and AI handoff](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/features/export/): Export a recorded bug as a ZIP with report.md, session.json, a manifest, transcript and assets, at Full, Standard, Compact or Minimal detail with live token estimates.

## Comparisons

- [All comparisons](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/compare/): Honest comparisons of Session Recorder with Jam, Marker.io, BugHerd, Userback and BrowserStack Bug Capture: who each suits, workflow differences and current paid pricing.
- [Session Recorder vs Jam](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/jam-alternative/): An honest comparison of Session Recorder and Jam: hosted bug-reporting workspace with integrations versus a free open-source extension that files GitHub issues from your own accounts.
- [Session Recorder vs Marker.io](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/compare/marker-io/): Compare Session Recorder and Marker.io for bug reporting: a website feedback widget for clients and UAT versus a free open-source recorder that files GitHub issues.
- [Session Recorder vs BugHerd](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/compare/bugherd/): Compare Session Recorder and BugHerd: pinned website feedback and a task board for agencies and client projects versus a free open-source recorder that files GitHub issues.
- [Session Recorder vs Userback](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/compare/userback/): Compare Session Recorder and Userback: a customer feedback platform with widgets, surveys and session replay versus a free open-source recorder for internal bug reports to GitHub.
- [Session Recorder vs BrowserStack Bug Capture](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/compare/browserstack-bug-capture/): Compare Session Recorder and BrowserStack Bug Capture, formerly Bird Eats Bug: a capture tool bundled with BrowserStack plans versus a free open-source recorder that files GitHub issues.

## Guides

- [All guides](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/guides/): Guides for using Session Recorder reports with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and ChatGPT, a browser bug report template, an example report, and what makes a bug report fixable.
- [Debug browser bugs with Claude Code](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/claude-code/): Record a browser bug — console, network, screenshots, voice — with a free open-source Chrome extension, then hand Claude Code an LLM-ready report it can read from your repo.
- [Debug browser bugs with Cursor](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/cursor/): Record a browser bug with a free open-source Chrome extension — console, network, screenshots, voice — and attach an LLM-ready report to Cursor&#x27;s Agent instead of retyping repro steps.
- [Debug browser bugs with Codex](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/codex/): Record a browser bug with a free open-source Chrome extension — console, network, screenshots, voice — and give Codex an LLM-ready report it can read locally or in a cloud task.
- [Give ChatGPT a complete browser bug report](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/chatgpt/): Record a browser bug with a free open-source Chrome extension and upload one self-contained report — console, network, screenshots, narration — to ChatGPT instead of pasting screenshots.
- [Browser bug reports for AI coding agents: what Claude Code, Cursor and Codex actually need](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/ai-bug-report/): A technical guide to building browser bug reports AI coding agents can actually fix: the eight signals that matter, why screenshots fail, temporal ordering, token budgets, deterministic trimming, redaction, and live browser vs recorded evidence.
- [Browser bug report template for AI coding agents](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/bug-report-template/): Copy a Markdown browser bug report template with reproduction steps, expected behavior, console errors and network evidence for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
- [What an LLM-ready bug report actually looks like](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/example-report/): A complete, sanitized example of the Markdown bug report Session Recorder exports for AI coding agents: timeline, network, console errors, annotations, narration, and every verbosity level.
- [Local-first design](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/local-first/): Session Recorder keeps recordings in your browser with no account or developer-operated backend. Transcription, AI summaries and publishing are optional and use your own providers.

## Setup help

- [Help](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/help/): Set up protected reports, one-click GitHub issues, and automatic AI summaries.
- [One-click GitHub issues](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/help/github/): Connect a repository once, then file an issue directly from a finished recording.
- [Automatic AI summaries](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/help/ai-summaries/): Turn recorded evidence into a concise issue draft when you click File GitHub issue.
- [Protected publishing](https://azimi.me/session-recorder-chrome-extension/help/cloudflare/): Publish reports to Cloudflare Pages and let your team sign in through Cloudflare Access.
